{"predictors": [
  {"name": "Inventory Turnover", "construction": "Cost of Goods Sold divided by Inventory", "rationale": "Firms with higher inventory turnover might be managing their resources more efficiently, leading to higher profitability and thus higher stock returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Cash to Total Assets", "construction": "Cash and Cash Equivalents divided by Total Assets", "rationale": "Firms with more cash could be more financially stable and less reliant on external financing, potentially leading to higher stock returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
  {"name": "R&D Intensity", "construction": "R&D Expenditure divided by Sales", "rationale": "Firms investing more in R&D might have a higher potential for future growth", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Employee Turnover", "construction": "Number of employees leaving the company divided by Total number of employees", "rationale": "Firms with lower employee turnover might have more stable operations and employee expertise, which could translate to higher returns", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Debt Maturity", "construction": "Long-term Debt divided by Total Debt", "rationale": "Firms with longer debt maturity might have lower financial distress risk", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Capital Expenditure Intensity", "construction": "Capital Expenditure divided by Total Assets", "rationale": "Firms with higher capital expenditure intensity might be investing more in their growth, potentially leading to higher stock returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Dividend Payout Ratio", "construction": "Dividends divided by Net Income", "rationale": "Firms with higher dividend payout ratios might be more profitable, which could lead to higher stock returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Operating Cash Flow Margin", "construction": "Operating Cash Flow divided by Sales", "rationale": "Firms with higher operating cash flow margins could be more financially healthy", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Age of Firm", "construction": "Current Year minus Year of Incorporation", "rationale": "Older firms might have more established market positions and thus higher stock returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Employee Satisfaction", "construction": "Employee satisfaction survey results", "rationale": "Firms with higher employee satisfaction might have more productive and loyal employees, leading to better operational performance and higher stock returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}
]}
